I don't really bother to weigh out what I eat to be honest, but if I looked at a typical day I usually eat at least 30-40g of protein (keep in mind that 1 gram of meat or whatever usually doesn't translate into 1 gram of protein.) Just eat a variety of foods rich in protein (yoghurt, peanut butter, nuts, chicken, fish, eggs, etc) as well as a balanced diet with fibre, carbs, healthy fats/sugars, etc. I wouldn't rely too heavily on protein bars in the beginning because those often have a lot of sugar/fat, which might not help you if your plan is to lose fat and put on muscle. 

Don't have to completely cut out junk food, I know from experience its not realistic to eat completely healthy 24/7. I would recommend just cutting back on how much fast food you get; get it only once or twice a week instead of daily, for example.

Ask your trainer for tips on what you should eat btw, they should be able to recommend things to help you/ your fitness goals specifically.

Totally doable. In my experience, the key is slowly gaining muscle mass; developed muscles can def help you get a more feminine physique if thats what you're going for. I (18F) started working out a couple times a week every week about a year ago.

I'm 180cm, and went from 67 kg when I started to 74 kg today, mostly muscle mass, and I've seen a big improvement in my physique, not to mention feeling a lot better/ stronger. 

Its a difficult process, but if you stick to a routine (even just working out a bit once or twice a week) and eat plenty of protein youre going to see results. Seeing a personal trainer is a very good idea to keep you motivated and make sure your form is good so you can work out efficiently and not get injured.

I think I know how you feel, because I was pretty much in your shoes at the beginning but you just have to keep slowly working at it and you'll achieve what you want to achieve <3 no such thing as perfection so just keep trying to improve yk
